title: User-controlled model name is written to logs without sanitization
reasoning: The route accepts request.model_name from the network request and passes it directly into route log messages. If model_name can contain newlines or control characters, a caller can forge or obscure log entries, which matters because this route crosses network and user-input trust boundaries and logs both normal and failure paths.
recommendation: Normalize model_name before logging, for example by replacing control characters/newlines, bounding length, or logging a validated canonical model identifier rather than the raw request field.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are linked for this feature, and the excerpt contains no coverage asserting log-safe handling of untrusted request fields.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a route-level or helper-level test that passes a model_name containing a newline/control character and asserts the emitted log record contains only a sanitized single-line value.
minimumFixScope: Sanitize or canonicalize request.model_name at the logging boundary in this router or in the logging helper functions.
